method: process RSS (psutil memory_info().rss; the Windows working set) sampled every 0.05 s from a second thread while handler.local() ran its stages on the kit day in one process (S3 GETs only; the status write goes to a stub client that only counts); a sample counts for every stage on the stack. A stage's peak includes the memory the process already held when it began.
stages_basis: AFTER the cut. The container 'lots' (the whole lots_days call) is left out of stages: it equals its largest member (lots_read) and would tie it.
process_peak_note: The after process peak (1459.1 MB) is above every stage peak (largest 1263.3): it is reached between the stages, in the handler's own table write after lots_days returns. Not cut here.

the_cut.what: read_window used to turn every account's rows of each lot, realized and trade partition into a pandas frame for each of the 8 account batches, then keep the batch's rows. It now makes the account mask from the account column alone and converts only the batch's rows from the arrow table; the whole-partition figures it reported (pre-2010 count, realized row count, source files) are taken from the arrow table as it passes. A table where a narrower conversion could change a dtype (an integer or boolean column holding nulls) or that names an index column takes the old full conversion.

hash_basis: sha256 of each output parquet file's bytes, written by handler.local() on the kit day: before = the producer files at HEAD 8658c32241, after = this order's commit. Frame equality (dtypes, index labels, values) of the cut read was also checked on the kit day for the four partitions read_window reads with the batch's first 1000 accounts.
